objections.claim: The only open finding in the critique is that the R1–R9 remainder lives solely in the FAFF-740 description; once this slice merges and FAFF-740 closes, the ordering constraints ("R9 before R1", "R7 before R1") are invisible to the pipeline, and the extension points this spec names (e.g. `--render-marker` after "exact source binding exists", R9's `--check-sources` before R1) have no tracked carrier.
objections.evidence: Methodology critique, "Surfaced deps: … Open, not in this ticket: the rest of the R1 to R9 remainder exists only in the FAFF-740 description … Recommendation for the maintainer: file R1 to R9 … with those blocking edges." Spec section 2 lists R1, R2, R7, R8, R9 as excluded with extension points but files only R4 (FAFF-1183).
objections.predicted_consequence: After merge, a future implementer picking up R1 (status markers) has no recorded dependency on R9 (exact source binding) or R7 (lint-refs markers), and can build the marker generator against the same drift-prone pointer model this ticket just patched — repeating the class of defect FAFF-740 exists to fix.

No other methodology objection. The critique finds the slice right-sized, correctly sequenced against FAFF-1183 and FAFF-824, and de-risked during prep; the contingency (peel prose fixes) is available but not triggered.

objections.claim: The DONE item asserts that running `--check-live` against the unrepaired `origin/main` ledger produces "exactly six stderr lines, naming the two source paths and four evidence targets listed in section 4". The spec does not define what "the unrepaired ledger" is as a concrete artifact, nor does it pin the exact expected error strings for the source-path cases. The liveness error messages for source paths are defined in section 3, but the DONE item references "the two source paths and four evidence targets listed in section 4" without restating them, and the section-4 list is prose, not a machine-checkable enumeration. A builder could run the check, get six lines, and still not know whether the *right* six lines were produced — or could "pass" by counting lines only.
objections.evidence: DONE item "`git show origin/main:L > /tmp/old.json && node V --check-live /tmp/old.json` exits 1 with exactly six stderr lines, naming the two source paths and four evidence targets listed in section 4".
objections.predicted_consequence: A build that produces six stderr lines but with a wrong message (e.g. a generic "path missing" message without the `record the move in source.current_path` suffix, or a duplicated line for one claim and a missing line for another) would satisfy the DONE item as literally written, because "naming the two source paths and four evidence targets" is not a byte-exact assertion. The test suite's negative cases cover only the *repaired* ledger with one mutation at a time; nothing asserts the full six-error output on the unrepaired ledger.

objections.claim: The DONE item "No claim in `L` has an `owner_issue` in `CLOSED_OWNER_ISSUES`" is decidable only if the constant is correct. The spec states the list contents in section 4, but nothing in the DONE criteria or scenarios verifies that the list itself matches tracker reality at build time. The spec's own assumption section says FAFF-1183 must be open and is checked in build step 1, but no analogous check exists for the eight closed-owner entries. A builder could copy the constant verbatim from the spec, run the test, see it pass, and ship — while the list is wrong (e.g. FAFF-743 was actually still open, or FAFF-734 was cancelled rather than done). The test would pass vacuously.
objections.evidence: DONE item "No claim in `L` has an `owner_issue` in `CLOSED_OWNER_ISSUES`"; section 4 "Owner-liveness assertion" states the list is "Done or Cancelled as of 2026-10-05" but provides no verification step.
objections.predicted_consequence: The build can pass every DONE item while the closed-owner list is factually wrong, because the only check is against the constant itself — the constant's truth is asserted in prose, never tested. The test's stated honest limit ("cannot notice an owner closing after merge") is acceptable; the gap is that it also cannot notice an owner that was *already* closed at the pinned date, and the spec provides no way to decide that.

objections.claim: The DONE item "Temporarily reverting one evidence target in `L` to `docs/evidence/README.md` makes that test file fail; restoring it makes it pass" is decidable in principle, but the spec does not say *which* evidence target to revert. The ledger has four evidence targets that were moved; reverting `l4-completion-claim`'s target to `docs/evidence/README.md` would produce a different failure than reverting `codex-observed-capability`'s target to `docs/architecture/codex-cli-observed.md`. The DONE item names one specific target (`docs/evidence/README.md`), which is the `l4-completion-claim` target, but the test's negative case in section 4 uses `codex-observed-capability`'s target. A builder could revert the wrong target, see the test fail for a different reason, and still satisfy the DONE item's letter.
objections.evidence: DONE item "Temporarily reverting one evidence target in `L` to `docs/evidence/README.md` makes that test file fail; restoring it makes it pass".
objections.predicted_consequence: The DONE item is ambiguous about which row to revert; the test suite's own negative case uses a different target, so the DONE item and the test disagree on the fixture. A builder following the DONE item literally reverts `l4-completion-claim`'s target, but the test's negative case would have used `codex-observed-capability`'s — the DONE item passes either way, so the check is vacuous.
